text: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Nishikawa's hyperbolic diffusion: iterate a first-order system Hiroaki Nishikawa (2007) introduces the first-order hyperbolic-system approach to steady diffusion, including second-order residual-distribution schemes. The 2010 extension unifies advection and diffusion. The date is the journal publication year, not the DOI's year. Implemented here: a periodic 1D, first-order upwind finite-volume baseline with SSPRK2. It demonstrates equivalent steady equations; it does not implement the original paper's second-order multidimensional RD constructions. Residual convergence and discretization error# The manufactured steady reference is sin(2πx), with zero mean on the periodic unit interval and forcing ν(2π)²sin(2πx). The initial mean fixes the constant null mode. Both equation residuals are measured; the gradient residual is scaled by 2π in the combined RMS diagnostic. A small residual does not eliminate the first-order upwind spatial error. N=32,64,128 checks that error separately. The manifest records steps and pseudo-time sizes, without a matched-cost speedup claim. Compare Thomas and multigrid, sparse preconditioning, and the physical diffusion gallery. Anisotropic diffusion, high-order face reconstruction, viscous Navier–Stokes coupling and the complete RD formulation are future extensions.
